newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares end up, underlying strength seen.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares end up, underlying strength seen.

text.p: Norwegian shares bounced back from early losses after a strong recovery on Wall Street. Dealers said that despite the overwhelming influence of the U.S. market on the Oslo bourse, there was underlying strength.
Oslo's Total share index advanced 0.36 percent to 1,105.28 points after a shaky start which saw the index lose more than one percent due to a hefty fall on Wall Street late on Thursday.
The market soon recovered to sit most of the morning session down 0.5 percent.
"The fact that we were just half a percent off given the U.S. drop last night is a good indication that we've got more gains ahead," said one broker.
Business was relatively thin at turnover of 889 million crowns, down almost 16 percent from a day ago.
Most traded share at 169 million crowns was Norsk Hydro, which relinquished two crowns to 346.50 crowns.

Fokus Bank gained 2.50 crowns to 58 crowns after the bank announced that the superior tax commission had ruled in its favour and the bank's tax-loss carried forward for 1996 had been increased to 2.2 billion crowns.
